The consultation and diagnostic scans were quick, smooth, and very well-organized.

The SMILE Pro procedure itself was over in less than 2 minutes and completely painless, simply followed the doctor’s instructions throughout.

What stood out was how comfortable and stress-free the whole process felt.

I’m extremely happy to finally be free from glasses and contact lenses, and especially relieved from the constant headaches caused by my refractive error (myopia with astigmatism).

Post-operative care was handled very well, with clear instructions on dos and don’ts and proper follow-up guidance.

[{"Name":"Julianna Carmenita","ProfilePicture":"https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/a/ACg8ocLr-d8GtwzJijy4QD4atSPoba-bPkQvGg5VaH5akSwKHSfqsg=s120-c-rp-mo-ba12-br100","Rating":1,"Description":"I am sharing this review because I genuinely want other pet owners to be aware of my experience with Dr. Shaw and the dental procedure performed on my dog, Penny.
Penny is a 3-pound dog who underwent a dental cleaning and multiple extractions under Dr. Shaw’s care. During the procedure, I received a call stating that six teeth needed to be removed, including a back upper molar located very close to the eye/orbital area. At no point was I advised to consider referral to a veterinary dental specialist despite Penny’s extremely small size and the complexity/risk associated with that area. I also was not informed of the serious potential complications that could occur.
Following the procedure, Penny developed worsening symptoms including swelling around the eye, pain, fever, decreased appetite, and visible distress. We returned multiple times seeking help. According to the medical records, the extraction site was documented as “difficult to see due to size of patient,” yet Penny was discharged without additional diagnostics or escalation of care.
The next morning, an emergency hospital immediately identified active purulent drainage coming from the extraction site. CT imaging and specialists later confirmed a severe abscess and infection tract extending from the extraction area into the orbital region behind Penny’s eye.
Despite emergency treatment and specialist intervention, the infection progressed to the point that Penny ultimately lost her eye.
This experience has been devastating emotionally, physically, and financially for our family. We incurred nearly $12,000 in emergency and specialty veterinary expenses as a direct result of these complications.
What was also deeply upsetting was the complete lack of personal accountability or compassion afterward. Dr. Shaw never personally called to check on Penny following the loss of her eye, and at no point did she apologize for what happened.
I understand that complications can occur in medicine, but I believe pet owners deserve full transparency about risks, especially in medically delicate cases involving very small dogs and complex extractions. I also was not informed of the serious potential complications that could occur.
Following the procedure, Penny developed worsening symptoms including swelling around the eye, pain, fever, decreased appetite, and visible distress. We returned multiple times seeking help. According to the medical records, the extraction site was documented as “difficult to see due to size of patient,” yet Penny was discharged without additional diagnostics or escalation of care.

Despite emergency treatment and specialist intervention, the infection progressed to the point that Penny ultimately lost her eye.
This experience has been devastating emotionally, physically, and financially for our family. We incurred nearly $12,000 in emergency and specialty veterinary expenses as a direct result of these complications.

My experience at Phoenix Clinics & Diagnostics, Magarpatta for a company-sponsored Annual Health Checkup booked via Medibuddy was poorly managed and time-consuming. There was a lack of advance communication, inconsistent information from staff, and significant waiting time due to doctor unavailability.
At a minimum, I expected:
•	Prior communication that breakfast is not provided
•	Clear information about doctor availability and test timings
•	Accurate clarity on tests included in my package
•	A logical test sequence that respects patients’ time
Unfortunately, none of this was handled well. Annual health checkups are time-sensitive, and this clinic did not value patients’ time. Based on my experience, I would not recommend this clinic due to inefficient processes and poor coordination.

Detailed Experience (For Those Who Want Full Context) -
I booked my Annual Health Checkup through Medibuddy at Phoenix Clinics & Diagnostics, Magarpatta, with an 8:00 AM slot and instructions to maintain 12 hours of fasting.
I reached the clinic at 8:10 AM. At that time, only one staff member was present, managing registration, assisting patients, and guiding the process. After a wait of about 15–20 minutes, the same staff member conducted my eye check-up. This raised a concern for me, as I was unsure whether eye check-ups should be conducted by a nurse rather than a doctor. Later, the same nurse also collected my blood sample.
By around 8:30–8:45 AM, two staff members were present. I was then asked to have breakfast and note the time, as I was informed that a second blood sample would be required after two hours. I mentioned that my previous company-sponsored health checkups did not usually involve a second blood sample, but the staff confirmed that it was required and asked me to return after breakfast.
When I asked about breakfast availability, I was informed that breakfast is not provided at the clinic, and I would need to arrange food outside. I was also told that I could return by 10:00 AM, as the sonography doctor arrives only after 10:00 AM. This information was not communicated before the appointment.
I informed the staff that I would quickly finish breakfast and return so that ECG and 2D Echo could be completed earlier, and the remaining tests could be done once the doctors arrived. I returned to the clinic by 9:00 AM and requested to proceed with the remaining tests. By then, 3–4 staff members were present, but I was asked to wait until my name was called.
During this waiting period, my doctor consultation was conducted, which felt awkward and unstructured, as key diagnostic tests such as ECG, 2D Echo, and sonography were still pending.
I waited patiently for about 45 minutes, following up in between. An ECG was eventually completed, and I was again informed that the sonography and 2D Echo doctors would arrive by 10:00 AM. Despite continuous follow-ups, the doctors arrived only around 10:30 AM, and sonography was performed then.
At around 10:45 AM, I was informed that the 2D Echo doctor was not responding to calls, and I was asked whether I was okay with proceeding with a TMT test instead. I preferred the 2D Echo, but after waiting for more than 2.5 hours, I agreed to proceed with the TMT test.
After completing the TMT test, I requested the second blood sample, only to be told that it was not included in my package. This was confusing, as I had been explicitly asked earlier to have breakfast and note the time specifically for a second sample. After reaching the back room were they call your number I was reminded that there would be a cost to my visit. I stepped away to see if i had the funds available and dismissed myself for a moment. The registration employee who already had my paperwork in hand was about to return it to me then as i reached out pulled it back and said with a smile, "and i can just shred this for you". I attended to my phone in that moment and stepped away... after concluding that i would simply return at another time so as not to hold up the One other customer in the clinic behind me i requested my paperwork back that i had filled out with my personal information (CPNI) She then said to me with a big smile " oh its fine we will shred it for you" once again. I stated then, "Its fine, i would like it back as it has my information and i wont be seen today, and i can dispose of it myself."

She then with a bit of an attitude tells me "Well no, i cant return it because it has a number written on it." Referring to the number i was given to be called up to the counter.... I then repeated what she was implying back to her to ensure i had heard her correctly.

"So your saying i cant have my paperwork back with my personal information on it, even though i wont be seen today, and the reason your denying me the paper is because it has a number written on it..?" She replied "yes". I retorted back to her how much i didn't think that was correct, and she answered me speaking over me and raising her voice.. As i walked out of the clinic after gathering my belongings and bag she very loudly said something about making a note of my behavior for the next time i return...

As you can imagine, i was quite surprised to hear that as if in a retaliatory fashion. What should i expect when i (IF I) ever return, simply for asking for my paperwork in return. Now the Legal aspect to this is at minimum i should have been offered a copy of the paperwork. But that was never offered. If it were for business purposes it would have been stated as such from the beginning, instead of that i was told "well shred it for you" as if a favor to me.

So no, i don't believe it was for business purposes, nor do i believe it was the process or regular procedure at this point. Her nonchalant approach to what i was stating was my concern was extremely unprofessional, and down right rude. Not to mention that chatter while waiting about how they deal with customers who complain about having to pay any fee at all. Her statement of "well how about you take this to another doctors office and you can pay them, see how it compares." Excuse me.. is this not a government facility or a community run outreach facility?

I expected the customer service to be at best simple, and uneventful, but rude, odd, and inconsiderate was not what i expected at all.

I hope the appropriate individuals are aware of this behavior and speech occurring in the waiting rooms of your clinic, and that your employees are much more professional when they are assisting and servicing the Clinics Customers. If you like i can provide the time, date and "NUMBER" that was so vitally important. And i hope that the many many other customers you assist are treated with more concern, understanding, and respect.

1/5 Stars as this was pertaining to one single employee. To the others who assisted me, thank you for being polite, and helpful.

If you’re a patient seeking care, don’t let my review scare you off. This is actually a great office, but I have one issue.

This is a great clinic like I said, I want to emphasize that part. The doctor and the nurses with me in the procedure room were ALL very good at coaching me and helping me to feel safe. And I did feel very safe, in part due to the wonderful bedside manner of the care team, and also the twilight sedation. I don’t want to minimize that or make it seem like this is a bad office. It’s a great office, and I would return there if I needed another abortion 100%. Also, while I was certain about my decision, I was indeed sad that I wasn’t ready for a baby. And every single person in this office was highly compassionate and understanding. They were all kind to me, they were all comforting, and I didn’t feel like just another body in their procedure room like I have at some other clinics in the past (for completely different procedures). I REALLY want to emphasize that I actually love this clinic.

However, as with a lot of women’s health clinics, I didn’t feel that most providers were honest with me about the pain. The doctor didn’t deny that it could be painful, instead he reassured me that the sedation and numbing helps a lot, which was comforting!

I can acknowledge that pain is different for everyone, and there’s no way to predict exactly how I would feel specifically. And some women don’t experience pain at all and that’s great for them. But I was repeatedly told that the worst it could potentially feel like was intense mentrual cramps or pressure. I know what severe mentrual cramps feel like, and the pain was a lot worse than that. I wouldn’t say it was unbareable, nor was it traumatizing. Again, I felt very safe in that office despite my nerves and the pain. But it was definitely quite painful. I’d rate it an 8/10 (years ago I had an IUD inserted and that was much worse at a 15/10). I’m sure that the twilight sedation and numbing shots helped a lot, and I have to say that the doctor did a wonderful job getting it done quickly. I also don’t remember everything, and I’m grateful for that. But I do remember crying and struggling to breathe due to the pain.

I know that medical providers are often told that minimizing the pain is the better way to go, and I can’t blame them for doing what they believe to be in my best interest. I know that everyone was only doing what they thought was best for me, I know the lying was done out of care. But minimizing pain is such an outdated habit. I would have much preferred the truth, I would have been able to handle myself better if I had been given the curtesy of an honest conversation. Instead I ended up freaking out mid-procedure. On top of the pain I feel so embarrassed. I keep thinking about yesterday and cringing, I feel so absolutely embarrassed.

I will say that everyone told me it’s alright, not to be embarrassed and that what I went through wasn’t easy. The doctor was especially kind to me regarding my distress.

I like this clinic, truly, but please just be honest with your patients. Lying is only ever harmful. I didn’t feel dismissed or uncared for. Just lied to. I really don’t appreciate that about women’s health. Patients have the right to make an informed decision, but it’s not an informed decision if we don’t know the truth about how bad the pain can be.

If you’re a patient reading this, absolutely still go here! Just know that it CAN be more painful than you might be lead to believe. [{"Name":"Ines Paulina Salazar Armenta","ProfilePicture":"https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/a-/ALV-UjVljb2ac-fqU-29BmsYKEiYHF7JFbHViyCDdqDQC4gKd9mO4z6I=s120-c-rp-mo-br100","Rating":1,"Description":"My experience with Dr. Michael Arntsen was extremely disappointing and honestly concerning. The first thing he said when he walked into the room was, “I don’t know why you’re on my schedule. I only see broken bones.” From that moment on, the entire interaction felt dismissive and disrespectful.
Patients seek medical care because they are in pain and looking for help. Regardless of whether an injury is considered “minor” or not, every patient deserves to be treated with professionalism, empathy, and respect. Instead, the tone used throughout the examination was rude and impatient, which made the entire visit uncomfortable and discouraging.
What is most troubling is the lack of empathy displayed during the encounter. Healthcare professionals hold a position of trust, and compassion is a fundamental part of that responsibility. Seeing someone with a medical license treat a patient in such a dismissive way is both surprising and disappointing.
As someone who works in healthcare myself, I understand that not every case may fall within a physician’s preferred scope. My heartfelt appreciation goes to Chief Nurse Jhansi Rani and the senior nursing team—Princy, Nandhini, Suji, and Bhavadharani. They were always attentive, caring, and ready to help whenever needed. Their patience and dedication really made a difference.

On 1/9/26 my boyfriend rushed himself to ValleyWise Med Center ER while visiting AZ with his 12y/o daughter. He had difficulty breathing, severe shoulder blade pain, & vomiting. Found out day 5 of 7, diagnosed w/ a widowmaker heart attack, something only about 5% survive. The interventional team who performed his emergency cardiac catheterization saved his life, & we are incredibly grateful. A few nurses — Terance, Quintin, Jesus, and Kristin — were attentive respectful & compassionate.

Unfortunately, much of the cardio team & overall care lacked communication & professionalism. We experienced condescending interactions, unclear answers, & poor coordination. Nursing care was inconsistent: bloody syringes left in his bed, trash/IV fluids on the floor where he was expected to walk, 20+ minute ICU call light delays, RXs not given as ordered, profanity @ the nurses’ station, urinals not changed despite limited mobility, & a 6hr wait for treatment of an infected IV site. He was placed NPO 3 consecutive days for a 2nd catheterization that was repeatedly postponed & ultimately canceled w/o clear communication. Discharge guidance was contradictory. 1 team told us he could fly home to FL in 2wks; another said absolutely not for 2months. We have no support system in AZ, which was repeatedly communicated. With no clear answers, we rented a car & drove 36hrs home, stopping every 45mins so he could walk.

Once in FL, we were unable to transfer critical RXs between ValleyWise & our pharmacy despite multi calls & management involvement. We were transferred repeatedly & hung up on, & had to wait until returning to Florida to obtain RXs.

We are thankful he survived. But the lack of communication, professionalism, & coordinated care made an already traumatic experience far worse. ValleyWise should be ashamed! If you must come here, bring a strong advocate w/ you.

I would like to express my sincere gratitude and appreciation to the entire team at *Phoenix Hospital Heart Care IC Colony & Chikuwadi* for the exceptional care and support extended to me and my family throughout my treatment journey,  right from the angiography to the bypass surgery and post-operative recovery.

Having been admitted to the hospital for 22 days and spending time in the ICCU on three separate occasions, I have experienced the dedication, pressure, and commitment of our doctors and healthcare professionals very closely.

A very special thanks to my  Cardiac Surgeon Dr. Ajay Pandey, whose calm, positive, and reassuring presence gave immense confidence to my family during a very difficult time. After the surgery, when he told my family, “The operation went off well and the heart will take its own rhythm,” it brought comfort, hope, and smiles to their faces. Those words will always stay with us. His patience in addressing every concern and the assurance he provided truly reflect not only his expertise as a cardiac surgeon but also his compassion as a doctor. Coming from Ayodhya, having served in Aurangabad, and now practicing in Mumbai, your journey reflects the incredible strength and excellence of India’s medical fraternity which is spread across boundaries. Hats off to you and your personal team of 8 doctors also for successfully completing such a complicated surgery in just three hours with remarkable skill and precision

I would also like to sincerely thank Dr. Vivek Vaghela (Internal Medicine Specialist) for carefully managing my medicines and guiding me with the right support during the post-operative phase. His attentive care and support have been deeply appreciated.

A special mention and heartfelt thanks to Cardiologist Dr. Vaibhav Bhastana for his timely help, guidance, and support throughout the process. His prompt decisions and assistance played a very important role in ensuring smooth treatment and care.

A special thanks to Dr. Jennifer Patekar, my physiotherapist, for her support, encouragement, and care throughout my recovery.

Lastly, I would like to appreciate the ICU & ICCU RMO, nursing staff, support staff, and the entire cardiac care team at Phoenix Hospital for their professionalism, kindness, and dedication.

Thank you once again for making my challenging journey much more manageable with your care and compassion.

Throughout this journey, I tried to carry positivity wherever I could, from celebrating Sister Juhi’s birthday in the ICCU to interacting with the young doctors and speaking about the dignity and importance of the nursing profession. I truly hope my spirit and willpower added warmth and encouragement to the environment, and I will always cherish the meaningful moments, smiles, and conversations shared during my stay.

In many ways, this journey truly felt like the story of a Phoenix bird l rising stronger, with renewed hope and life.

With sincere gratitude,

Your Over- Enthusiastic Patient,
